briefdescription.para: Store-registered holder for the Drogon PostgreSQL client used when DB_ASYNC=true.

detaileddescription.para: This header defines one small class that owns a Drogon database client. The client is kept in a shared pointer so several parts of the server can refer to the same underlying connection pool. The class also contains two helpers: one that builds the client from the database settings, and one that writes those settings into the keyword/value string PostgreSQL expects.

WHY THIS FILE MATTERS IN THE SERVER: This file is the home of the asynchronous (non-blocking) database client. When the DB_ASYNC setting is on, the server startup code (Server::run()) calls AsyncDbClient::createClient() and stores the result in the Store, which is the server's shared service registry. Later, each database controller method fetches this object from the Store and passes the Drogon client inside it to asyncdb::execSqlCoro(), which runs the SQL without occupying a worker thread. Tests can register a fake (or empty) client through Store::replaceObject(). Without this file there would be no way for the async controllers to reach PostgreSQL, and the whole DB_ASYNC code path would be unreachable; the older synchronous connection pool would remain the only working option.

CONCEPTS TO LEARN (for beginners):
C++20 coroutines: https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/language/coroutines
Drogon DbClient: https://drogon.docsforge.com/master/database/
std::shared_ptr (shared ownership of one object): https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/memory/shared_ptr
RAII (tying a resource's lifetime to an object's lifetime): https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/language/raii
PostgreSQL connection strings: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/libpq-connect.html#LIBPQ-CONNSTRING
